name: Seat & Seat Mounts
description: Fixed-back FIA/SFI racing seat on seat-specific side brackets, bolted to a welded floor mount / reinforcement plates, with optional rear seat-back brace to the harness bar.

components.name: Driver racing seat (fixed-back, halo/head-surround)
components.description: Fixed-back composite or aluminum containment seat that locates the driver relative to the harness, FHR device and cage. Choose a seat with 6-point (dual-sub) harness slots and integrated head surround; the seat label must be within its validity date.
components.location: Driver side, H-point x ≈ 1.75, y ≈ 0.33, z ≈ +0.37, as low as possible on the floor.

factory.name: ZL1 / 1LE Recaro performance bucket (power/manual), on factory 4-bolt rails
factory.notes: Factory seats are not race seats: no sub-belt slots, recliner mechanism; delete for road racing.

raceOptions.name: FIA 8862-2009 seat (e.g. Racetech, Sparco, OMP 8862 models)
raceOptions.notes: FIA 8862-2009 = 10-year validity from label; best side-impact protection. Camaro GT4.R used a Racetech seat + Schroth harness.

raceOptions.name: SFI 39.2 aluminum/composite containment seat
raceOptions.notes: US oval/road-race style aluminum seats; require proper back brace and mounting per maker.

specs.Validity: Read "not valid after" date on label (8862 & 8855-2021: 10 yr; 8855-1999: 5 yr)

hardware.spec: M8 x 1.25 x 20–25 mm hex/button head + flat washer + nyloc/spring washer (Sparco kit: M8 bolts + locking nuts)
hardware.grade: ISO 8.8 min (10.9/12.9 in many FIA kits)
hardware.notes: M8 torque per Schroth bolt chart (25 N·m); follow seat maker instructions if different. Use seat-maker spacers to avoid crushing composite. Checked 2026-10: Sparco publishes no torque for the 50002 side-mount kit (M8 x 1.25 bolts plus locking nuts), and FIA 8855 leaves fasteners to the seat maker. 25 N·m is the standard class 8.8 M8 value (Atlas Copco). If the bolts thread into bonded inserts in a composite shell, do not exceed the maker's value. Motorsport UK guidance requires at least 4 points with bolts of at least 8 mm (https://www.motorsportuk.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Seat-Installation-Guidance-v4.pdf). Remains typical.

installNotes: Mock-up seat with driver in full gear (helmet + FHR) BEFORE final cage harness-bar height is set.
Seat as low and rearward as allows steering/pedal reach; check helmet clearance to roof bars (≥ 2 in typical).
Confirm the seat label date covers the full racing season.
inspection: Inspect shell for cracks at bracket holes; re-torque seat bolts each event.

sources.title: Motorsport UK – rule changes, seat/harness lifing
RACER – Chevy unveils Camaro GT4.R racer
SCCA Time Trials – Full Safety Rules

components.name: Seat side-mount brackets (seat-specific, FIA approved)
components.description: Steel or aluminum L-brackets bolted to the sides of the seat shell, then to the floor mount/sliders. For FIA seats the brackets must be the seat manufacturer's homologated brackets.
components.location: Left and right of the seat shell, z ≈ 0.37 ± 0.26, bottom at y ≈ 0.21.

raceOptions.name: Sparco side-mount brackets + hardware kit
raceOptions.notes: Kit: 4 × M8x1.25x25, 8 × M8x1.25x20, 8 locking nuts, 8 washers.

specs.Material: Steel 3–5 mm or aluminum per maker

hardware.spec: M8 x 1.25 or 3/8-16 bolt + nyloc + large washers
hardware.notes: M8 per Schroth chart; for 3/8-16 Grade 8 use 35–44 ft-lb typical. Never mount the seat with fewer than 4 bolts per seat. Checked 2026-10: the M8 value comes from the Atlas Copco class 8.8 table; the 3/8-16 Grade 8 range comes from standard SAE dry charts, 40-52 ft-lb (https://www.quadratec.com/jeep_knowledgebase/article-105.htm), reduced for nyloc and washers. CORRECTED: the old single 18.4 ft-lb would under-clamp a 3/8-16 bolt.

installNotes: Set seat height with brackets first, then drill/weld the floor mount.
inspection: Check bracket bolt torque every event.

components.name: Seat floor mount (welded tube frame or seat base)
components.description: Structure tying the seat brackets to the chassis. Race builds weld a tube/box frame or FIA weld-on seat mounts to the floor and rocker; bolt-in Camaro-specific bases (Sparco 600SB284L, Brey-Krause, Planted SB284) use the factory seat studs and are good for lightly modified cars.
components.location: Driver floor pan between rocker and tunnel, x ≈ 1.55–2.00, y ≈ 0.19–0.22, z ≈ 0.10–0.64.

factory.name: Factory seat rail studs/holes (4 per seat)
factory.notes: Reusable mounting points for bolt-in bases.

components.name: Seat-mount floor reinforcement plates
components.description: Steel plates welded/bolted to the floor under each seat-mount point to spread crash load (FIA seat anchorage: ≥ 40 cm², ≥ 3 mm). Bolted versions sandwich the floor with a matching backing plate.
components.location: Driver floor at each seat-mount corner (x ≈ 1.58/1.98, z ≈ 0.13/0.61).

specs.Size: ≥ 40 cm² x 3 mm (e.g. 45 x 90 x 3 mm or 88 x 46 x 3 mm)

hardware.spec: 3/8-16 or M10 x 1.5 bolt + nyloc through backing plate
hardware.notes: M10 torque from Schroth chart (50 N·m); seal plate to floor with seam sealer. Checked 2026-10: 50 N·m matches class 8.8 M10 (49 N·m, Atlas Copco). For 3/8-16 Grade 8, standard dry charts give 40-52 ft-lb (https://www.quadratec.com/jeep_knowledgebase/article-105.htm), so up to 44 ft-lb is acceptable. Remains typical.

installNotes: Seal plates to floor (seam sealer) to stop water intrusion.

components.name: Seat-back brace (to harness bar / cage)
components.description: Rear support from the seat back to the harness bar/cross tube, preventing the seat back from deflecting rearward in a rear impact. Required by many aluminum-seat makers and common with SFI 39.2 seats; FIA seats use the homologated mounting only – do not add braces that change load paths unless the maker permits.
